processing: Green tea made under a local organic tea standard, DB61/369-2005; the individual making steps are not widely published.
harvest_season: Spring is the usual season for Shaanxi greens; dates specific to this tea are not widely published.
appearance_dry: Even leaf with a jade-green colour.
taste_profile: A high, long aroma and a mellow, full taste that holds up over several steeps.

brewing.notes: General settings for a Shaanxi green. It takes repeated steeps well, so do not overextend the first.

vintage_note: As with other Shaanxi greens, it is usually bought as the current year's spring harvest and drunk within the year. The geographical indication covers several grades, so ask which one you are getting.
description:
Pingli Nüwa Tea is the geographical-indication green of Pingli County in southeast Shaanxi, centred on misty Nüwa Mountain, which gives it its name.

The registered area is big: 11 townships and 50 villages at 300 to 2,717 metres, so the name alone tells you little about a garden's altitude. Production follows a local organic standard.

Expect a jade-green leaf, a clear liquor and a high, long aroma over a mellow body. It takes several steeps, more than many delicate greens.

Selenium dominates the marketing, with reported levels of 0.52 to 3.52 ppm. Taste comes first when choosing; ask for the grade, the township and the harvest date.
history: Pingli has a long tea-growing history, though little is dated before modern times. On 15 November 2010 China's Ministry of Agriculture approved geographical indication protection for the name, covering a reported 150,000 mu and 2,700 tonnes a year.
